data.detect#Detect:
go-filesystems/detect is a pure-Go (no cgo, no libblkid) blkid-style prober and driver-opener registry. It reads fixed, bounded windows of an image to identify the filesystem, then dispatches to a registered driver. The core depends only on go-filesystems/interface and the standard library; drivers are wired in by blank-importing an adapter.
import ( "github.com/go-filesystems/detect" _ "github.com/go-filesystems/detect/fat32reg" // registers FAT12/16/32 ) t, err := detect.Detect(r, size) // probe only, e.g. "fat32" fs, t, err := detect.OpenFile("disk.img") // probe and open Open returns ErrUnknown when no signature matches and ErrUnsupported when a type is detected but no driver is registered for it.
data.encrypted-containers#Encrypted container:
A filesystem may sit inside a full-disk-encryption container. Containers are wired in like drivers, so a program that never opens encrypted images links no cryptography: the core contains none. The adapter module detect/fdereg registers them with a blank import:
import _ "github.com/go-filesystems/detect/fdereg" fs, t, err := detect.OpenSecret(r, size, []byte("passphrase")) fs, t, err := detect.OpenFileSecret("disk.img", secret) fs, t, err := detect.OpenContainer(detect.LUKS, r, size, secret) // name the container Container Backend Notes LUKS 1 and 2 go-fde/luks detected by its header BitLocker go-fde/bitlocker read-only; password, recovery password or .BEK VeraCrypt / TrueCrypt go-fde/veracrypt read-only; opened by name only, because its header is ciphertext Unlocking. OpenSecret probes the registered containers first. On a match it unlocks the container and probes the plaintext for a filesystem. When nothing matches it opens the image as Open does. Without a secret, Open and OpenFile return ErrEncrypted wrapped with the container’s name and do not probe the ciphertext (a BitLocker To Go volume starts like FAT32). VeraCrypt has no probe: OpenContainer(detect.VeraCrypt, ...) opens it by name. FileVault 2 is not a container layer: APFS encrypts inside the filesystem and opens it with its own OpenFDE. The containers’ own documentation is at go-fde.github.io/docs.

data.drivers#Drivers:
The 15 filesystem drivers available today (plus oci, a read-only image-as-filesystem overlay, and detect, a type-probing dispatch registry — both listed separately below since neither targets an on-disk format in the same sense as the rows in this table).
Module Read Write Format Label Symlinks Quota Snapshots Encryption On-disk format Platform apfs ✅ ✅ ✅ — ✅ — ✅ ✅ Real APFS on-disk (kext-mountable), GPT-aware macOS / iOS btrfs ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✕ ✕ — Single-device, CRC32c (btrfs-progs ≥ 5.x) Linux exfat ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✕ — — — exFAT Windows / removable ext4 ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✕ — ✕ ext4 — extents, 64-bit, flex_bg, dir htree, metadata_csum (CRC32c) Linux fat32 ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✕ — — — FAT32; FAT12 / FAT16 (resize keeps the FAT type) cross-platform ffs ✅ ✅ ✅ — ✅ ✕ ✕ — NetBSD/OpenBSD FFSv1/FFSv2 — thin re-export of ufs BSD hfsplus ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ — — — HFS+ / HFSX (Mac OS Extended), big-endian catalog + extents-overflow B-trees macOS (legacy) iso9660 ✅ ✕ ✕ — ✅ — — — ISO 9660 / ECMA-119 + Rock Ridge (names/perms/symlinks) + Joliet (UCS-2 names) cross-platform (optical) ntfs ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✕ — — — Minimal in-image blob model — NOT the real NTFS on-disk format; a separate read-only reader parses genuine NTFS Windows squashfs ✅ ✕ ✅ — ✅ — — — SquashFS 4.0 read-only archive; gzip/xz/zstd/lzo/lz4 blocks + fragments Linux uefi ✅ ✅ ✅ — — — — — OVMF/EDK2 NvVar variable store; time-based authenticated writes firmware (UEFI) ufs ✅ ✅ ✅ — ✅ ✕ ✕ — UFS2 (FreeBSD 14.x) read+write; UFS1 read; NetBSD/OpenBSD FFSv1/FFSv2 (via ffs alias module) BSD xfs ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ — ✕ XFS v5 (CRC32c, ftype) Linux zfs ✅ ✅ ✅ — ✅ ✕ ✅ ✅ read-only Single pool, single-vdev writer (multi-vdev/RAID-Z read-only) illumos / BSD / Linux oci ✅ ✕ — — ✅ — — — OCI/Docker image layers merged read-only (whiteouts, opaque dirs, hardlinks) any (image, not disk) Legend: ✅ supported by the driver · ✕ not yet implemented (the format has the feature) · — not applicable. Read = open & inspect · Write = mutate in place · Format = create a fresh image. Quota / Snapshots / Encryption reflect driver support, not just the on-disk format’s capability.
Reading a range of a large file. A server that answers a read of a few bytes (NFS READ, SFTP) should not load the whole file. Since the audit of 2026-11-05, apfs v0.6.0, btrfs v0.5.0, hfsplus v0.6.0, ntfs v0.4.0, ufs v0.5.0, xfs v0.5.0 and zfs v0.5.0 implement filesystem.Opener (OpenFile(path) returns a file whose ReadAt reads only the extents or blocks of its window; holes read as zeros). A 1 MiB read at 66 MiB of a 72 MiB file allocates 0 bytes through it on hfsplus, apfs, btrfs, xfs and ntfs, 5.5 MB on ufs and 1.1 MB on zfs, against 75 to 538 MB through ReadFile. A compressed (LZNT1) stream of a real NTFS volume is still decoded whole, once, on the first read. go-filesystems/nfs bounds the whole-file fallback at 64 MiB (NFS3ERR_IO above).
oci bounds every input-driven allocation before it happens (DefaultLimits(): manifests 16 MiB, 16 GiB for a whole image); an excess returns an error wrapping safeio.ErrTooLarge.
Also in the org: detect, a blkid-style type prober and driver-opener registry that dispatches to the drivers above — it isn’t an on-disk format itself, so it has no row.

data.apfs#apfs:
Apple File System.
Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-filesystems/apfs Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/apfs API reference: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-filesystems/apfs See the module’s README for full, up-to-date details.
data.not-implemented#Not implemented: Snapshot creation gated behind an Apple-private entitlement Some encrypted-container fsck stages are Apple-private Writing to a FileVault volume (it opens read-only); per-file-key (hardware) encryption
data.status#Status: Read Write Format Label Symlinks On-disk format ✅ ✅ ✅ — ✅ Real APFS on-disk (kext-mountable), GPT-aware
data.supported#Supported: Real APFS read: FS-tree traversal, multi-extent files, xattrs, sealed volumes Snapshot read (OpenSnapshot) Write & format kext-mountable containers FileVault software encryption: write (FormatContainerEncrypted) and, since v0.4.0, read-only open (OpenFDE, OpenFDEFromBlockDevice, and the …Limited variants that bound key derivation for untrusted images). Only the FS-tree nodes flagged OMAP_VAL_ENCRYPTED and the file extents with a crypto_id are decrypted; the container metadata is read as the plaintext it is. A wrong passphrase (ErrWrongPassphrase) and a refused keybag (ErrLimit) are told apart with errors.Is. GPT + Apple DMG output POSIX special files Container resize (Resize)
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: Every size in an image is a claim, bounded before it is made: file reads by the backing store’s real size, each extent must lie inside the image, sparse holes and a declared size past the last extent by 1 GiB of invented zeros (safeio.ErrTooLarge; stream larger sparse files with FileReaderAt), and a decmpfs uncompressedSize by 1 GiB.

data.btrfs#btrfs:
Copy-on-write Linux fs with snapshots and subvolumes.
Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-filesystems/btrfs Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/btrfs API reference: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-filesystems/btrfs See the module’s README for full, up-to-date details.
data.not-implemented#Not implemented: Snapshots, send/receive, multi-device/RAID, quotas and reflink are not implemented
data.status#Status: Read Write Format Label Symlinks On-disk format ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Single-device, CRC32c (btrfs-progs ≥ 5.x)
data.supported#Supported: Read/write files Directories, rename, symlinks MBR/GPT auto-detect
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: Every allocation, walk and recursion sized from a value on the image is checked against what the format can produce before it happens: a compressed extent is at most 128 KiB (the kernel’s BTRFS_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED), a zstd window 128 KiB, overlapping file extent items are refused, and a chunk stripe_len must be exactly 64 KiB.

data.exfat#exfat:
Extended FAT for large media.
Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-filesystems/exfat Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/exfat API reference: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-filesystems/exfat See the module’s README for full, up-to-date details.
data.not-implemented#Not implemented: No POSIX symlinks, permissions or ACLs (not in exFAT)
data.status#Status: Read Write Format Label Symlinks On-disk format ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✕ exFAT
data.supported#Supported: Read/write files Directories, recursive delete, rename Bare images + MBR/GPT Times (filesystem.TimesReader, v0.5.0): creation and modification to 10 ms, access to 2 s, each with its UTC-offset byte (a clear OffsetValid bit reads as time.Local, as the spec says); no change time. An invalid date is “not recorded”. Checked against an image written by macOS newfs_exfat
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: Every allocation a value in the image can size is bounded before it happens: a cluster buffer is allocated only after the cluster’s last byte has been read, and a directory is at most 256 MiB. A hostile image gets an error, not an out-of-memory kill.

data.ext4#ext4:
Linux ext4 — extents, 64-bit, journaling, metadata_csum.
Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-filesystems/ext4 Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/ext4 API reference: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-filesystems/ext4 See the module’s README for full, up-to-date details.
data.not-implemented#Not implemented: Some cross-check tests require mke2fs Not every kernel ioctl / obscure feature is implemented
data.status#Status: Read Write Format Label Symlinks On-disk format ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ext4 — extents, 64-bit, flex_bg, dir htree, metadata_csum (CRC32c)
data.supported#Supported: Read/write files (extents, sparse writes) Directories, rename, symlinks metadata_csum (CRC32c) writes Online grow / shrink / resize (Grow, Shrink, Resize) CheckImage / RepairImage hooks GetFlags/SetFlags ioctls MBR/GPT auto-detect Times (filesystem.TimesReader, v0.5.0): access, modification and change to 1 ns when the inode’s _extra words fit (their two epoch bits extend the seconds), 1 s otherwise; creation from i_crtime only when the inode is large enough, so 128-byte ext2/ext3 inodes have none. All-zero is “not recorded”. Checked against images made by mke2fs and debugfs set_inode_field
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: Every allocation and walk sized from a value on the image is checked against what the image can hold before it happens. ReadFile is capped at the smaller of the declared filesystem size and DefaultMaxReadSize (1 GiB), changed with SetMaxReadSize and refused with ErrTooLarge; larger files are read with OpenFile. Overlapping extent leaves are refused and the extent tree depth is at most 5.

data.fat12-16#FAT12 and FAT16:
The variant is decided by the count of data clusters, as the Microsoft FAT specification says (below 4085 is FAT12, below 65525 FAT16), never by the FAT12/FAT16 label. The root directory of these two is a fixed region after the FATs, and a FAT12 entry is 12 bits packed, so one can straddle a sector boundary. Both are handled; Info.Type says which one a volume is.
Writing works (v0.7.0): files, directories, rename, truncate, the label and positional writes. The fixed root directory never grows, so a create in a full root fails with directory is full and changes nothing; long-name entries count against its capacity. After every mutation scenario the image passes fsck_msdos -n.
Resizing works (v0.8.0) while the volume keeps its FAT type. Shrink refuses when a cluster past the new end is in use and leaves the FAT at its size; Grow works in place, even when the FAT itself must grow (v0.10.0): the FAT is made bigger and the fixed root and the data shift forward by the difference, from the end backwards in 64 KiB chunks. Cluster numbers do not change, so no FAT entry, directory entry or chain is rewritten. Sizes are whole sectors. A resize that would change the type (crossing 4085 or 65525 clusters) is refused with ErrResizeType: “growing to N clusters would make this FAT16 volume FAT32; copy it into a new image of that size with CopyResized”. A grow too small to keep the clusters the volume has once its FAT has grown is refused too. Both wrap ErrResizeFAT, and a refused resize changes nothing (ErrResizeFATFull is no longer returned). Crash safety (v0.11.0): a grow that does not move the layout, and a shrink, leave the old or the new size at any interruption. A grow that moves the layout (FAT12, FAT16 and FAT32) is journaled and rolled forward: it keeps a record in the last sector of the image, and the next Open (or OpenReader over a writer) finishes an interrupted grow before serving the volume. Every interruption therefore ends as the old volume (the record was never written) or the grown one, fsck_msdos-clean with every file intact. Until that Open, a tool that does not know the record sees a half-moved layout between the first move and the boot-sector write; over a read-only reader an interrupted volume is refused (ErrReadOnlyReader). A grow too small to leave the record a free sector past the moved layout is refused (ErrGrowTooSmall). Chunks of 256 KiB or more are flushed (Sync) around their record; below that the order holds for a process crash or an I/O error, not a power loss mid-move. Together with detect v0.4.0, which reports fat12 and fat16, such an image opens exactly like a FAT32 one.
data.fat32#fat32:
FAT with 32-bit allocation. Since v0.6.0 it also reads FAT12 and FAT16 volumes, and since v0.7.0 writes them: what newfs_msdos -F 12|16 and mkfs.vfat produce below about 33 MiB.
Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-filesystems/fat32 Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/fat32 API reference: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-filesystems/fat32 See the module’s README for full, up-to-date details.
data.not-implemented#Not implemented: No POSIX symlinks (not in FAT32) Resizing a FAT12 or FAT16 volume to another FAT type: done by CopyResized instead, never in place A crash-proof in-place grow that moves the layout (needs a journal)
data.status#Status: Read Write Format Label Symlinks On-disk format ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✕ FAT32, FAT12, FAT16 (read/write/resize; FAT12/16 resize keeps the type)
data.supported#Supported: Read/write files Directories, recursive delete, rename Bare images + MBR/GPT Volume label (Labeller) Times (filesystem.TimesReader, v0.12.0): write time to 2 s, access time as a date (24 h), creation time to 10 ms; no change time. FAT stores the local wall clock, read here in time.Local. A zero or invalid field is “not recorded”. Checked against entries written by newfs_msdos and mtools mcopy -m Resize (filesystem.Resizer) CopyResized (v0.9.0): the resize FAT12/16 cannot do in place (another FAT type), or one that leaves the source untouched. It formats a new image of the wanted size (the FAT type follows from the cluster count as mkfs.fat decides, or is forced; impossible combinations are refused) and copies the whole tree: long names, directories, contents, attributes, timestamps and the label. The source is only read. A tree that does not fit, or a root with more entries than a FAT12/16 fixed root, is refused before the destination is written fsck-clean images (v0.5.1): fsck_msdos -n and fsck.vfat -n exit 0 on what the driver writes. The .. entry of a directory under the root holds cluster 0, and the FSInfo free count and next-free hint are exact at format and kept current while the image is written Format to a path (Format) or into any io.ReaderAt + io.WriterAt, such as a buffer in memory (FormatImage) — what the playground uses to make its sample image in the browser
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: Every allocation a value in the image can size is bounded before it happens: a cluster buffer is allocated only after the cluster’s last byte has been read, the sector size is 512..4096, and a directory is at most 2 MiB. A hostile image gets an error, not an out-of-memory kill.

data.ffs#ffs:
NetBSD/OpenBSD Berkeley Fast File System (FFS) — a thin re-export of ufs, since FFSv1/FFSv2 are the same on-disk format as UFS1/UFS2.
Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-filesystems/ffs Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/ffs API reference: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-filesystems/ffs See ufs and the module’s README for full, up-to-date details.
data.status#Status: Read Write Format Label Symlinks On-disk format ✅ ✅ ✅ — ✅ NetBSD/OpenBSD FFSv1/FFSv2 (= UFS1/UFS2), via the ufs driver
data.supported#Supported: Everything the ufs driver provides, under an import path that matches how NetBSD/OpenBSD callers think of the format (ffs.OpenFile, ffs.Open, ffs.OpenRW — thin aliases of the ufs entry points).
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: ffs re-exports ufs, so it inherits its bounds on an untrusted image: a read grows its buffer with the blocks it reads, and a sparse file is limited to DefaultMaxFileBytes (1 GiB), changed with SetMaxFileBytes; a read over it fails with an error wrapping ufs.ErrTooLarge.

data.hfsplus#hfsplus:
Apple HFS+ (Mac OS Extended) and its HFSX (case-sensitive) variant.
Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-filesystems/hfsplus Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/hfsplus API reference: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-filesystems/hfsplus See the module’s README for full, up-to-date details.
data.journal#Journaled volumes:
Since v0.9.0 the write path knows about the HFS+ journal (Apple TN1150). It does not write transactions itself, and macOS replays a journal that holds some over whatever was written around it, so:
A journaled volume with an empty journal (start == end, what a clean unmount leaves) is written directly. The journal info block, the journal and the journaled attribute are left as they were, so macOS replays nothing at the next mount. A journal with transactions in it, or one that cannot be verified (a bad checksum, a journal outside the volume or on another device), is refused by OpenWritable and OpenFileWritable with the typed error ErrJournaled. Nothing is written, and OpenFileWritable closes the file. Test it with errors.Is(err, hfsplus.ErrJournaled). Read-only Open is unchanged: it reads a journaled volume whatever its journal holds. A caller that gets ErrJournaled can fall back to it. Volumes made by Format and Mkfs are not journaled. Do not write an image that is mounted. Neither the driver nor the system that mounted it knows about the other’s changes. Write an image nothing else has open.
data.status#Status: Read Write Format Label Symlinks On-disk format ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ HFS+ / HFSX, big-endian catalog + extents-overflow B-trees
data.supported#Supported: Read/write files Directories, rename SetLabel / Symlink / Truncate (optional Labeller / Symlinker / Truncater capabilities) MBR/GPT auto-detect Times (filesystem.TimesReader, v0.7.0): creation, content modification, attribute modification (Mac OS X’s change time) and access from the catalog record, to 1 s, GMT seconds since 1904-01-01 (Apple TN1150). A date of 0 is “not recorded”, and so is the root folder’s. Checked against an image written by macOS newfs_hfs
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: Every size in an image is a claim. A fork’s logical size is bounded by the image size and every extent it uses must lie inside the image before the buffer is made; with the size unknown the buffer grows with the bytes the reader delivers. The B-tree leaf-chain walk is bounded by image size / node size.

data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-filesystems/iso9660 Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/iso9660 API reference: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-filesystems/iso9660 See the module’s README for full, up-to-date details.
data.iso9660#iso9660:
ISO 9660 / ECMA-119 optical-disc filesystem (.iso images), with Rock Ridge.
Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.
data.not-implemented#Not implemented: Write/format — ISO 9660 is a read-only format; mutators return ErrReadOnly Rock Ridge deep-directory relocation (CL/PL/RE) Multi-extent files
data.status#Status: Read Write Format Label Symlinks On-disk format ✅ ✕ ✕ — ✅ ISO 9660 / ECMA-119 + Rock Ridge (names/perms/symlinks) + Joliet (UCS-2 names)
data.supported#Supported: Primary Volume Descriptor scan (CD001), logical block size, root record Directory-record parsing + per-sector padding-aware directory walk Contiguous single-extent file reads (multi-sector) Rock Ridge (SP/NM/PX/SL): real case-preserved long names, POSIX modes, symlink targets (ReadLink), and CE continuation areas Joliet (UCS-2 long names via the supplementary volume descriptor), used when Rock Ridge is absent Path resolution by real (Rock Ridge / Joliet) name, with a case-insensitive fallback for base ISO names
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: Every length in an image is a claim. A file’s or directory’s length is bounded by the image size and its extent must lie inside the image; with the size unknown the buffer grows with the bytes the reader delivers and claims above 1 GiB are refused. A directory extent is at most 16 MiB.

data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-filesystems/ntfs Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/ntfs API reference: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-filesystems/ntfs See the module’s README for full, up-to-date details.

data.ntfs#ntfs:
Windows NT filesystem.
Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.
Lightweight, test-oriented. Use a real NTFS implementation for on-disk compatibility.
data.status#Status: Read Write Format Label Symlinks On-disk format ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✕ Minimal in-image blob model — NOT the real NTFS on-disk format
data.supported#Supported: Read/write files (blob storage inside the image) Directories, recursive delete, rename In-image free-list reuse In-image Grow / Shrink / Resize and compaction (Compact, FragmentationStats, Layout) A separate read-only reader parses genuine on-disk NTFS: LZNT1 decompression, named streams (ADS), $REPARSE_POINT symlinks/junctions, $ATTRIBUTE_LIST, volume label Times on that real-NTFS reader (filesystem.TimesReader, v0.5.0): creation, modification, MFT change and access, each a 100 ns UTC FILETIME from $STANDARD_INFORMATION ($FILE_NAME only as a fallback); a FILETIME of 0 is “not recorded”. Not on the NTFSIMG1 in-image driver

data.squashfs#squashfs:

Implements filesystem.Filesystem. No cgo, no root.

A read over it fails with an error wrapping ufs.ErrTooLarge, before anything is allocated.

data.interface#Interface:
Every driver implements the contract defined in go-filesystems/interface (package filesystem):
type Filesystem interface { Close() error ReadFile(path string) ([]byte, error) ListDir(path string) ([]DirEntry, error) Stat(path string) (Stat, error) WriteFile(path string, data []byte, perm os.FileMode) error ReadLink(path string) (string, error) MkDir(path string, perm os.FileMode) error DeleteFile(path string) error DeleteDir(path string) error Rename(oldPath, newPath string) error } Optional capabilities are probed via type assertion:
Labeller — volume label get/set. Resizer — grow/shrink (returns ErrShrinkUnsupported where shrink is impossible). TimesReader (v0.6.0) — the read side of the times MetadataSetter.Chtimes writes.
data.smb-set-times#Setting times over SMB:
smb v0.10.0 also writes them. A SET_INFO FileBasicInformation request applies the access and write times the client sets, through MetadataSetter.Chtimes. A time of 0 keeps that time unchanged; -1 freezes it and -2 resumes it, per handle (MS-FSCC 2.4.7, MS-FSA). Freezing needs a driver that also implements TimesReader: -1 on a Chtimes driver without it answers STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED in every mode below.
A time that cannot be stored (the creation time, a change time sent alone, or an access or write time on a driver without Chtimes) follows the per-share option smb.UnstorableTimes(TimePolicy):
Mode Effect TimesIgnore (zero value, default) Success; the field is dropped, as Samba does, so Explorer and robocopy /COPY:T copies work. TimesRefuse STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED; nothing is applied. TimesLog As TimesIgnore, plus a slog line on Server.Logger (default slog.Default()), with the path escaped. See the package reference for the full API, including DirEntry and Stat.
data.timestamps#Timestamps:
Stat has mode, size and inode, and no times. TimesReader returns all four POSIX times in one call:
type TimesReader interface { Times(path string) (FileTimes, error) // Atime, Mtime, Ctime, Btime } if tr, ok := fsys.(filesystem.TimesReader); ok { ft, _ := tr.Times("/report.txt") mtime := ft.Mtime.Or(time.Now()) // an explicit fallback, never a zero } Each time is a Timestamp, not a time.Time:
A missing time is not a zero one. FAT has no change time and several formats have no birth time. The zero Timestamp means “not recorded”, and there is no accessor that returns a bare time.Time without saying whether one exists (Get() (time.Time, bool)), so it cannot be written out as 1601 or 1970 by accident. Resolution is reported (Resolution()): FAT keeps the write time to 2 s, the access time to one day and the creation time to 10 ms; HFS+ keeps 1 s; NTFS 100 ns; ext4 and the host 1 ns. Same compares two times at the coarser of the two. One call, not four: the driver resolves the path once. It is on the Filesystem, by path, not on File: the callers (NFS GETATTR, SMB QUERY_DIRECTORY, SFTP stat, WebDAV PROPFIND) have a path, and a File is a snapshot of the size. Implemented by osfs v0.4.0 and fat32 v0.12.0, exfat v0.5.0, the real-NTFS reader of ntfs v0.5.0, ext4 v0.5.0 and hfsplus v0.7.0; the SMB, NFS, SFTP and WebDAV servers report them to clients when the driver has them.

data.changes#Changing the image: In the explorer you can upload, make folders, rename, copy and delete, on fat32, exfat and ext4. The other drivers refuse writes. The file you dropped is never written. A change lands in a copy-on-write layer under the drivers, in the tab’s memory (at most 256 MiB), and inside a LUKS container it lands encrypted. Download the modified image then saves the original with the changes in it, in the same format. Opening another image, or leaving, asks first while changes are not downloaded.
data.encrypted#Encrypted images:
A LUKS1 or LUKS2 container (go-fde/luks) is recognised by its header, and the page asks for its password. The engine unlocks it and opens the filesystem in the payload: detected, or the one chosen in the list. The facts then read e.g. ext4 in LUKS. A wrong password is refused, and the form stays to try again.
An APFS FileVault volume (apfs v0.4.0, OpenFDEFromBlockDeviceLimited) is recognised by the keybag its container names, at offset 0 or in a GPT’s APFS partition. When the volume cannot be read without its key, the page asks for the password, and the facts then read apfs in FileVault. A FileVault volume opens read-only. In both cases the key derivation the header or keybag asks for is bounded before any work is done.
data.explorer#Open in the explorer: Once an image is open, open in the explorer loads the go-fileshare explorer in a same-origin frame. It is fetched only then (4.1 MB compressed), and browses the image the way it browses a fileshare server, over WebDAV. None of its requests reach a network. The page hands each one to the engine, which answers it with go-filesystems/webdav over the open image. Closing the explorer unloads it.
data.how-it-works#How it works: The Go engine runs in a Web Worker. Its io.ReaderAt reads the dropped file with FileReaderSync.readAsArrayBuffer(file.slice(off, end)) — a synchronous read that the File API allows only in workers — so the drivers’ synchronous reads never block the page, and the image is never loaded whole. A block cache (64 KiB blocks, LRU, 16 MiB) turns a driver’s many small metadata reads into a few block reads; file contents bypass it. A checkbox on the page turns it off for comparison. The page is plain HTML, CSS and a few KiB of JavaScript, talking to the worker with three coarse requests: open, list a directory, read part of a file.
data.playground#Playground:
https://go-filesystems.github.io/playground/ — open a disk image in your browser. The page says which filesystem it is, lets you browse the tree, view small files and download any file. Everything runs in WebAssembly in your browser: nothing is uploaded.
No image at hand? Make a sample FAT32 image: the page formats one in memory with fat32.FormatImage, writes a few files into it, opens it again through detect, and lets you download it.
data.resize#Copy to a resized image:
A volume in the tab cannot be truncated, so a FAT image cannot grow in place, and a FAT12/16 root directory cannot grow either. On a FAT image (not one inside LUKS), the Resize row asks for a new size (1 to 256 MiB, the bound that applies to changes), a FAT type (FAT12, FAT16, FAT32, or let the size decide, as mkfs.fat does) and an optional label. fat32’s CopyResized (v0.9.0) then formats a new image of that size in memory and copies the whole tree into it, your changes included. The page shows the type and size it made, and you can download the copy or open the copy in place of the image. The open image is only read.
A request that cannot be met is refused with the reason, and nothing is made: the tree does not fit (ErrCopyNoFit), the root directory needs more entries than a FAT12/16 fixed root holds (ErrCopyRootFull), the size cannot be formatted as the chosen type (FAT32 needs at least 65525 clusters), or the size is outside the bound. The size is checked before any memory is taken.
data.safety#Safety:
The image is untrusted input: every answer is bounded (entries per listing, bytes per read), a driver panic becomes an error, a request that takes more than 30 s restarts the engine, and names from the image are shown as text, never as HTML.
A LUKS header is untrusted too: it says how much key derivation unlocking costs. The engine refuses a header that asks for more than 2²² PBKDF2 iterations, or for Argon2 beyond 16 passes or 1 GiB, before deriving anything (go-fde/luks OpenFromLimited). An unlock gets 180 s.
The password goes to the engine in the tab for one open. It is not stored and never sent anywhere. The page empties the field, and the engine clears its copy once the container is unlocked or refused.
Source: https://github.com/go-filesystems/playground
data.what-it-opens#What it opens: Filesystem Found Viewing and downloading fat32, exfat, ext4, iso9660, squashfs at offset 0, by detect streamed in 4 MiB pieces (filesystem.Opener) ntfs, hfsplus, ufs at offset 0, by detect read whole, files up to 64 MiB apfs, btrfs, xfs, zfs in a disk image’s GPT or MBR table, through a read-only block device read whole, files up to 64 MiB The Filesystem list chooses the driver. Detect it, the default, asks detect; when nothing opens at offset 0, the four disk-image drivers are tried in turn. Choosing a filesystem forces that driver, for an image detect gets wrong or cannot recognise.
